decisive_items: Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL (normal, <0.023 ng/mL)
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR
total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA)
response.rationale: R2 is the most specific diagnosis, directly supported by markedly elevated troponin I and ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and Q wave, with coronary angiography confirming occlusions. R7 is a broader MI label, while R1 is a syndrome, R6 is an ECG-pattern-specific term, and R3/R4/R5 are anatomical or broad categories.

rejected.why: Acute coronary syndrome is a broad syndrome; the evidence points to myocardial infarction specifically.
Only describes LMCA occlusion, not a diagnosis; lacks acute MI evidence.
Only describes RCA occlusion, not a diagnosis; lacks acute MI evidence.
Coronary artery disease is a chronic condition, not the acute presentation.
STEMI is a nonstandard term and overemphasizes ECG pattern; troponin and occlusion are more definitive.
Myocardial infarction is correct but less specific than acute myocardial infarction.
